QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
QQQ’s 252-return DFA H fell from 0.520 (Nov 6) to 0.465 (Nov 17), below the independent finite-variance reference of 0.5. Despite R²=0.934 on sampled scales, one line fits poorly across scales 8–63. Short/long H=0.472/0.626 suggests a crossover or temporary volatility shift.

H fell 0.0028/0.0315 over 1/5 observations. The prior-30 standardized deviation of −0.70 isn’t a significance test because windows overlap. Magnitude H=0.755 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

Hill alpha rose from 3.20 (Nov 5) to 3.49 (Nov 16–17). Lower means heavier fitted tails; higher means thinner, if the model fits. The 1,000-return window uses k=100 and x_min=0.02043 in absolute log-return units. The idealized independent-sample standard error, 0.349, understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.58/3.02, not a confidence interval. Plateaus can occur without new top-100 returns. These are uncertain descriptions, not a crash forecast.

interpretation.text:
SOXX’s 252-return DFA H fell from 0.485 (Nov 10) to 0.410 (Nov 17), below the independent, finite-variance reference of 0.5. Despite R²=0.926 on tested scales, one line fits scales 8–63 poorly: 0.401 short versus 0.595 long may reflect crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Magnitude H=0.769 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H fell 0.010/0.075 over 1/5 observations. It was 1.92 standard deviations below its prior-30 average, not a significance test because windows overlap.

Using 1,000 returns, Hill alpha rose from 2.985 (Nov 13) to 3.031 (Nov 16–17; k=99, x_min=0.03898 absolute log-return units). With a suitable model, lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails. The independent-return standard error (0.305) understates uncertainty with dependence. The 5%/15% cutoff estimates (3.538/2.567) aren’t confidence bounds. Plateaus are normal when new returns miss the largest extremes. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SPY.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On Nov 17, SPY’s 252-return DFA H=0.495 was near 0.5, the reference for independent returns with finite variance. Despite R²=0.959 on supplied scales, slopes of 0.469 (8–20) and 0.575 (25–63) make one exponent fit poorly across 8–63, possibly reflecting crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Magnitude H=0.678 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H fell 0.0011/0.0057 over 1/5 observations. Its prior-30 z-score was +0.19, not a significance test because windows overlap. H/alpha went from 0.448/3.252 (Oct 12) to 0.527/3.400 (Nov 6) to 0.495/3.374 (Nov 17).

Hill uses 1,000 returns (~4 years), k=99, and x_min=0.01453 in absolute log-return units. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. Independent-return SE (alpha/√k)=0.339 understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% estimates (3.362/2.944) aren’t confidence bounds. Alpha can plateau when new returns miss the top 99 without implying a static market. These are uncertain descriptions, not a crash forecast.
